fixer.title: base: avoid Base64 encoding string-chain amplification

cases.mechanism: The old loop appended four individual character strings per three source bytes, producing millions of concatenations and a retained string chain for multi-megabyte resource payloads.
cases.symptom: Large Base64 resource reads incurred excessive retained memory and synchronous encoding latency before their RPC response could be sent.
cases.fixedBehavior: The encoder now allocates one exact-size byte buffer, writes Base64 character codes directly, and converts to a string once, eliminating per-character string-chain construction.
cases.evidence: Deleted base line 443 is one of four single-character appends performed for every three input bytes; the neighboring deleted loop therefore creates O(input bytes) string nodes. Added line 434 allocates one exact-size byte result which is filled in place and converted once. The synchronous encoder is called on complete filesystem results before resourceRead replies in src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/agentHostProtocolClient.ts:3254-3257, placing that work directly on large-file RPC latency.
